title: LinkAudit
description: Result of `rebar doctor --output json`: {findings, finding_count, pre_repair_tag_oid, locks, lock_findings}. Each finding is a net-active blocking edge that disagrees with the structural link rule — `kind` is `ancestor-blocking` (an endpoint is an ancestor of the other), `mis-escalated` (the resolver returns a different pair than the one recorded, in which case resolved_source/resolved_target carry it), or `unreadable` (an endpoint could not be reduced). After a `--repair` pass each finding also carries `repair_status` (`repaired` or `unrepairable`) and, when unrepairable, a `repair_reason`. `pre_repair_tag_oid` is the tracker OID tagged `pre-doctor-repair` before the first write, empty on a read-only run. `locks` is the read-only lock-health report — one row per lock leg (the tickets write lock's fcntl and mkdir legs, the clock lock, the enrichment drain lock) giving `state` (held/free/absent/unknown), the stamped legs' v2 ownership stamp in `holder` (the mkdir leg and the enrichment drain lock) plus its rendering in `holder_description`, the holder-liveness verdict `pid_state` (same-host only; `unprobeable (...)` elsewhere), the hold age `held_seconds`, and `staleness`. `lock_findings` carries only the legs whose staleness is `stale` (no live process claims them); doctor never reclaims a lock, and `--repair` performs no lock action. Exit 0 = nothing outstanding, 1 = link findings or stale locks remain.
